subject.title: Feature: Built-in pace-aware rate limiting for autonomous agents

question: Should OpenClaw add a core pace-aware quota policy for autonomous agents, and should the first phase be visibility-only or enforcement-capable?
rationale: The request would add Anthropic-specific usage semantics, new status/session_status output, possible persisted pace state, new config defaults, and autonomous throttling behavior that could change existing agent execution.

options.title: Visibility first
options.body: Normalize pace/usage windows into status and session_status without blocking agent work, then revisit enforcement after the contract is proven.

options.title: Opt-in core enforcement
options.body: Design a new pace policy, config schema, persistence model, and upgrade tests before implementing any autonomous throttling.

options.title: Plugin or hook boundary
options.body: Keep core to usage visibility and add only the missing plugin/provider hook if an external policy plugin cannot implement the behavior today.

recommendation.title: Visibility first
recommendation.body: Normalize pace/usage windows into status and session_status without blocking agent work, then revisit enforcement after the contract is proven.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses status, agent-loop, config, and provider-usage boundaries where steipete has recent adjacent history and likely routing context.
